messages.author: c050f543c4f75e77
messages.subject: orthogonalize() not working
parts:
Hi,

I'm new in R. Some (or many) of my questions may be too primitive. Apology for that in advance.

I am trying to run an SEM model with residual-centered latent two-way interaction. In the tutorial, the first command is the orthogonalize(), which I tried and it is showing an error. 

Here is my codes:
library(lavaan)
library(semTools)
library(dplyr)

colnames(data)

#subset of the whole dataset, ti = moderator, kn = IV & ag = DV
data_small <- data %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  select(ti1, ti2, ti3, ti4, kn1, kn2, kn3, kn4, ag1, ag2, ag3, ag5)
  

#Orthogonalize the items of IV and mod
orthogonalize(data_small, 1:4, 5:8)

I go the following error:
Error: <haven_labelled> * <haven_labelled> is not permitted

Am I doing something wrong? How can I fix it and proceed?


Regards,
Husain

messages.author: c050f543c4f75e77
messages.subject: Re: orthogonalize() not working
parts:
Hi Mauricio,

I sorted the problem out. It was not about updates of the packages. It was the issue with dataset format. My imported dataset was a SPSS file. Somehow the function does not work on the SPSS dataset. So, I converted the file into .csv format and everything went smoothly afterwards. 

I hope the developers will fix this format problem soon. Social science researchers like me are heavily dependent on SPSS and Stata (because of the user-friendly interface compared to R). I still do most of the basic analyses in SPSS (mainly because I am new in R). Once I'll be fluent in the R language, it can be my primary data analysis tool.  

Cheers.
Husain


Kind regards,
Husain Akareem, PhD
Assistant Professor
International University of Japan

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: orthogonalize() not working
parts: I tried the read.table function to import the SPSS dataset.
read.table() is for text files, not SPSS data sets.
How do you import SPSS files in R?

library(foreign)
?read.spss

I usually use something like:

dat <- read.spss("path/to/file.sav", use.value.labels=FALSE, to.data.frame=TRUE)
